question.:question/problem: Given that $f(x)=-ln⁡20+\frac{1}{3}{e}^{x}$, the slope of the tangent line at $x=-ln⁡\frac{11}{3}$ is{{field-1}}.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The derivative of ${e}^{x}$ is just ${e}^{x}$ itself. On the other hand, $-ln⁡20$ is a constant, so its derivative is $0.$

First, using the addition rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-ln⁡20+\frac{1}{3}{e}^{x}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-ln⁡20)+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{3}{e}^{x}) \\  & =0+\frac{1}{3}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{x}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{e}^{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent at $x=-ln⁡\frac{11}{3}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=-ln⁡\frac{11}{3}} & ={(\frac{1}{3}{e}^{x})\,|}_{x=-ln⁡\frac{11}{3}} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{e}^{-ln⁡\frac{11}{3}} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot \frac{3}{11} \\  & =\frac{1}{11}.\end{aligned}
$$
